subject: Post-incident clarity note, RCA summary, and validation plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <j.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: May 6th service degradation — closure note and next steps

Hi James —

Thanks again for your patience while our team completed the investigation into the May 6th inference availability degradation that affected a subset of requests on your account. We wanted to close the loop and offer a concise summary plus a plan for validation and follow-up.

Short summary: an autoscaling race condition in the model pool controller caused an elevated error rate for 22 minutes during the 03:05–03:27 UTC window on May 6. Impact: your production inference requests experienced increased 502/503 responses and token-level timeouts; estimated customer-facing error rate peaked at ~8% for affected routes.

Next steps we will deliver this week:
- RCA summary and timeline (attached)
- Action items and owners with ETA (attached)
- A short verification plan for your team to confirm remediation in a staging window

I’ve attached the RCA summary and the timeline CSV. Marissa and Hannah are copied for any follow-up operational questions or to schedule a joint verification session.

Would you prefer a short technical walk-through (30 minutes) or just the doc for asynchronous review?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-rca-acme-summary.pdf (PDF, 86 KB)]
From: James Park <j.park@acmecloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: May 6th service degradation — closure note and next steps

Thanks, Sergio —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. A couple quick asks so our security and SRE teams can sign off:
1) Can you provide a clear timeline with timestamps (UTC) of the detection, mitigation, and closure actions?
2) Who are the owners for the code change and the operational guardrail to prevent recurrence?
3) We’ll likely ask for a verification window in our staging environment — can you propose a few times next week?

If you can include a short summary of what changed in the autoscaler logic, that will help our reviewers. We prefer an async doc first; if there are open questions we can schedule the 30-minute session.

Thanks,
James
SRE Lead, AcmeCloud
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <j.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: May 6th service degradation — closure note and next steps

James — thanks for the questions. Attached are: (1) a concise RCA PDF that addresses the timeline and root cause, (2) a CSV with per-minute telemetry during the window, and (3) a verification checklist you can run in staging. Below is the core content pulled from the RCA for your reviewers.

RCA (executive summary):
- Root cause: race condition in the model pool controller when two scale-up events for the same tenant overlapped; a transient state allowed one allocation to return partial metadata and the request router to mark the node as unhealthy, producing 502/503 responses.
- Contributing factors: unusually bursty traffic pattern from a scheduled job for tokenization; a lower-than-expected TTL on cached allocation metadata that caused repeated allocation refreshes.
- Detection: internal alerts triggered at 03:07:12 UTC when error-rate crosses configured threshold; first customer-reported ticket at 03:09 UTC.
- Mitigation: automated rollback to previous allocation policy at 03:18 UTC and an emergency hotfix to serialization logic deployed at 03:24 UTC. Full service returned to baseline at 03:27 UTC.

Timeline (UTC):
- 03:05:10 — traffic burst begins (scheduled tokenization job)
- 03:07:12 — internal error-rate alert triggered
- 03:09:03 — AcmeCloud reported degraded responses (ticket 7921)
- 03:12:40 — on-call began targeted tracing and identified allocation failures
- 03:18:06 — temporary rollback of allocation policy (reduced concurrency)
- 03:24:55 — hotfix deployed to controller serialization path
- 03:27:11 — error rates returned to normal

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Fix: controller serialization guard and atomic allocation state (Hannah Schmitt) — ETA: 2027-05-14
- Guardrail: increase metadata TTL and add idempotent allocation checks (Marissa Cole) — ETA: 2027-05-20
- Monitoring: add tenant-specific surge detection and alerting (Platform team) — ETA: 2027-05-28
- Compensation/credits: we will follow Redwood’s incident credit policy; Marissa will coordinate credit estimate and send separately.

Verification plan for AcmeCloud staging:
- Redwood proposes two 60-minute windows next week (May 17, 10:00–11:00 PDT or May 19, 13:00–14:00 PDT) to run a simulated tokenization burst while we monitor allocation behavior. We will provide a verification checklist and telemetry extracts in advance.

Attachments: redwood-rca-acme-summary.pdf, may06-timeline.csv, verification-checklist.md

Please review the attached and let us know which verification slot you prefer. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute technical walk-through after your review.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-rca-acme-summary.pdf (PDF, 86 KB)]
[Attachment: may06-timeline.csv (CSV, 12 KB)]
[Attachment: verification-checklist.md (MD, 4 KB)]
From: James Park <j.park@acmecloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: AcmeCloud Support <support@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident clarity note, RCA summary, and validation plan

Sergio —

Received the RCA and attachments; thanks for the level of detail. We’ll review internally and take the May 19, 13:00–14:00 PDT verification slot.

A couple follow-ups for your ops team ahead of the window:
- Can Hannah share the hotfix diff and a short note on why the serialization change prevents the race?
- Please provide the telemetry keys/queries we should run during the simulation (latency, error-rate, allocation-health).

We’ll confirm participants for the joint test by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
James
SRE Lead, AcmeCloud
